root_cause.text: The openvswitch vport code lacks an upper bound check on the size of the upcall PID array set via netlink, allowing a large array that overflows the fixed-size reply buffer and triggers a BUG_ON crash.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids() accepts any non-zero multiple of sizeof(u32) with no upper bound" and the patch adds a check rejecting PIDs > nr_cpu_ids, plus the precomputed size in ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(). The crash occurs in ovs_vport_cmd_set because the skb allocated with NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE cannot hold the full PID array, causing nla_put() to fail and hit BUG_ON(err < 0).

vuln_statements.explanation: This check only validates alignment and non-zero length, lacking an upper bound on the upcall PID array size. This allows an arbitrarily large array to be accepted, leading to allocation of excessive memory that later overflows the fixed-size netlink reply buffer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The new function ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids (lines 348-376) only validates that nla_len(ids) is non-zero and a multiple of sizeof(u32), but does not impose any upper bound on the array size.
